defect.description: A NETRC path is still expanded under the home directory: os.path.expanduser(f"~/{name}") turns NETRC=/etc/ci/netrc into a path like /home/user//etc/ci/netrc, so a NETRC file outside the home directory (an absolute path, or one starting with ~) is never found and no credentials are returned; only the default NETRC_FILES names should get the ~/ prefix.

review_items: netrc_auth.py:17 always prepends ~/ so an absolute NETRC path is expanded under $HOME and corrupted; use the NETRC value directly
test uses a relative NETRC name with HOME=tmp_path, which masks the bug; add an absolute-path test
netrc_auth.py:11-17 absolute NETRC path silently corrupted to $HOME/absolute/path by the expanduser on line 17
empty-string NETRC passes the `is not None` check, so $HOME/ is parsed and raises NetrcParseError; use `if netrc_file:`
test sets NETRC to a bare filename, which masks the absolute-path bug; add an absolute-path test
KeyError catch around expanduser is a false shield for absolute NETRC paths; loop body does not match NETRC semantics
votes.evidence_quote: When `NETRC` holds an absolute path like `/etc/custom.netrc`, this produces `~//etc/custom.netrc`, which expands to `$HOME/etc/custom.netrc`. The absolute path is corrupted.
votes.justification: The review points to the `os.path.expanduser(f"~/{name}")` call in get_netrc_auth. It explains that an absolute NETRC path gets prefixed with `~/` and resolves under $HOME, so the real file is never found. That is the known defect.
